source: The first close export from alesievauctions.com, supplied by the maintainer on 2026-09-10 as `test-auction-with-cascade-bids.csv`. Converted to a fixture without changing a value.

files.headers: Item | Category | Starting Bid | Current Bid | Bid Count | High Bid | Average Bid | Median Bid | Low Bid
files.shape: one row per lot, from the site's own database
files.why: PRICES ARE DUMMY DATA. The maintainer confirmed on 2026-09-10 that this is a sample extract showing which ROWS AND COLUMNS a close carries, not a record of an auction that happened. So this fixture pins GRAMMAR AND ROUTING and must never be used to pin a number against prices.csv — there is no auction to reconcile it with. It is the second fixture in this repo that cannot be replayed against a recorded row; the alesievauctions.com listing page in fixtures/auction-open was the first, for the same reason (the source was brand new).
files.seasonEvidence: Three names decide it, and they are exactly the season-discriminating names inferSeasons exists to find: `Ioun Stone Warden Wrath` is 2027's Display Name for `1k Bonus`, `Shirt of Cat's Gift` for `2k Bonus`, and `1st Codex of the Familiar` for `8k Bonus`. inferSeasons returns ['2027'] with no tie. There is no 2027 row in auctionMetadata yet, so a real import of this file would have to promote the auction first.
grammar: `(N of M)` is a LOT NUMBER — lot N of M lots of the same item. Trailing only, and stripped before anything else reads the name. Without this rule 0 of 163 lots resolve; with it (and the two below) 116 do.

A name containing a comma is wrapped in literal double quotes INSIDE the CSV quoting: the raw field is `"""5,000 GP Gold Bar"" (1 of 9)"` and the cell value is `"5,000 GP Gold Bar" (1 of 9)`. The quotes sit outside the name and inside the lot marker.
`X,000 GP Gold Bar` is X `1,000 GP Gold Bar` tokens. `1,000 GP Gold Bar` is the only gold bar tokenMetadata has ever held, in every season.
A trailing `10x` (`Alchemist's Ink 10x`) means what a leading `10x` means — the same rewrite forumClose.gs already makes.
files.routing: Column B states the destination. `Augment - Player` -> contextItems `token`, `Augment - Grunnel` -> contextItems `grunnel`, `Withheld` -> contextItems `withheld` with no price, `Onyx` -> the onyx tab. Everything else (`Trade`, `Premium`, `Bonus`, `Ultra Rare`, blank) is an ordinary priced lot.
notInTheSample: Withheld rows — the maintainer said they arrive in a later revision of the export.
Onyx rows — possible in these auctions but absent here.
An `Augment - <kind>` other than Player or Grunnel.
files.namesColumnBCannotSplit: `Pick Your Purple` (34 lots) and `Random Ultra Rare` (9 lots) are BOTH labelled `Ultra Rare`, and they belong in different files. A PYP is a buyer choosing any Ultra Rare — a market observation, and it goes in the price spine as `Ultra Rare` (a new EXCEPTIONS entry). A Random Ultra Rare is a lucky dip, and all 21 of its recorded appearances in contextItems.csv are ONE aggregated `token` row. So the split is by NAME, and it is what keeps `random ultra rare` deliberately out of EXCEPTIONS.
files.ignoredColumns: Starting Bid, Bid Count, High Bid, Average Bid, Median Bid, Low Bid. `Current Bid` is the ending bid. Note that `Average Bid` here is a per-lot bid statistic sitting beside a genuine winning-bid column — forumClose.gs REFUSES any file carrying that header, correctly for its own source, which is why this export gets its own reader rather than going through forumReadStaging.
